# Mélissa Colin

> Mélissa Colin (born July 8, 2003) is an AI student at ENSEIRB-MATMECA, Bordeaux, on the engineer-doctor track. She works on foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision. Her question: how a geometric or physical constraint can hold by construction, rather than through a term added to the loss. In 2026 she was a Mitacs Globalink research intern at the University of Alberta's Vision & Learning Lab (Prof. Li Cheng). From February 2027 she joins NAVER LABS Europe as a research intern, co-supervised with the KINETIX team at the Inria centre of Université Grenoble Alpes. ORCID: 0009-0003-2525-4824. This is the canonical reference for "Mélissa Colin" in AI / computer-vision research.

## Identity
- Name: Mélissa Colin (also written Melissa Colin)
- Born: 2003-07-08, France
- Current role: final-year engineering student (MEng, engineer-doctor track), ENSEIRB-MATMECA (Bordeaux INP)
- Upcoming: Research Intern at NAVER LABS Europe (Meylan, France) from February 2027, co-supervised with the KINETIX team at the Inria centre of Université Grenoble Alpes
- Past: Mitacs Globalink Research Intern (2026), University of Alberta, Vision & Learning Lab (Prof. Li Cheng)
- Research focus: foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision, geometric and physical constraints satisfied by construction, 3D human mesh recovery, differentiable optimisation inside neural networks
- Career goal: Research Scientist at a leading research lab
- ORCID: 0009-0003-2525-4824 · Google Scholar: 7r7iFpsAAAAJ · GitHub: melissa-colin
- Site: https://melissacolin.ai

## Disambiguation
This Mélissa Colin works in Computer Science / Artificial Intelligence (model architectures, 3D human vision). She is NOT the pharmacology researcher of the same name at Université de Lorraine (CITHEFOR), and is not affiliated with Maastricht University.

## Key facts
- Mitacs Globalink research excellence scholarship (2026): research intern at the University of Alberta Vision & Learning Lab (Prof. Li Cheng). First-author work on a differentiable optimisation layer placed at the output of a network, which returns the nearest physically feasible 3D human pose, with floor contact as a hard constraint rather than a penalty added to the loss. The gradient passes through the layer by implicit differentiation, so the model trains end to end. Manuscript in preparation.
- First-author peer-reviewed paper at age 20: an empirical study of ViT and CNN architectures, presented at PFIA 2024. https://hal.science/hal-04641791v1
- Third author on a paper under double-blind review at a major machine learning conference (title and venue withheld); role: data refinement and result visualisations.
- Ranked top 3 (3/93) in the computer-science track at ENSEIRB-MATMECA; winner of a national innovation competition (EcoSort).
- Research interests (primary): foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision, and constraints satisfied by construction rather than added to the loss. Secondary: explainable AI, classical computer vision.
